positive.prompt: Our workflows duplicate provider mechanics; design a shared capability without moving domain policy into it.
Deepen this module by simplifying its public interface and choosing a stable test seam.
Refactor these shallow service boundaries and correct the dependency direction.

negative.prompt: Implement the approved feature as a thin vertical slice and run repository-native tests.
Diagnose the intermittent failure by building a reproducible red loop.

evals.prompt: Two account flows duplicate payment-provider setup and error handling. Propose a design that improves reuse without letting the shared service own domain state.
evals.expected_output: A deep public capability boundary with explicit inputs, structured failures, policy/mechanics ownership, public tests, and an incremental migration path.
expectations: The proposal identifies callers, invariants, owned state, dependency direction, and a public seam before naming files.
Domain policy, authorization, state transitions, and user-facing recovery remain with orchestration.
Provider mechanics use explicit inputs and structured outputs without hidden database access.
Tests observe behavior through the public seam rather than shared-service internals.
Migration moves one caller at a time and verifies behavior before removing the old path.
